questions.question: Which policy of Lord Dalhousie was a significant political cause of the 1857 Revolt?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Doctrine of Lapse**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Doctrine of Lapse** was an imperialistic annexation policy implemented by **Lord Dalhousie**, who served as the **Governor-General of India** from **1848 to 1856**.
 
• According to this policy, any Indian princely state under the **suzerainty** of the **British East India Company** would be annexed if the ruler died without a direct natural male heir.
 
• It fundamentally challenged Indian traditions by refusing to recognize **adopted heirs** as legal successors to the throne, which caused intense resentment among the ruling classes.
 
• Major princely states annexed under this doctrine included **Satara (1848)**, **Jaitpur (1849)**, **Sambalpur (1849)**, **Udaipur (1852)**, **Jhansi (1854)**, and **Nagpur (1854)**.
 
• The annexation of **Jhansi** following the death of **Raja Gangadhar Rao** was a direct catalyst for **Rani Lakshmibai** to join the **Revolt of 1857** to reclaim her kingdom.
 
• This policy, combined with the annexation of **Awadh** on grounds of misgovernance in **1856**, created an atmosphere of fear and distrust, serving as a primary **political cause** for the uprising.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Dual Government**:

 
 
• Introduced by **Robert Clive** in **Bengal** following the **Battle of Buxar** and the **Treaty of Allahabad (1765)**.
 
• It divided the administration into **Diwani** (revenue rights) held by the British and **Nizamat** (administrative duties) held by the Nawab.
 
 
 
• **Ryotwari System**:
 
 
• A land revenue system introduced by **Sir Thomas Munro** and **Alexander Read** in **1820**, primarily in the **Madras** and **Bombay** Presidencies.
 
• It involved a direct settlement between the government and the **ryots** (individual cultivators) without the use of intermediaries like Zamindars.
 
 
 
• **Vernacular Press Act**:
 
 
• Proposed by **Lord Lytton** in **1878** to restrict the freedom of Indian-language newspapers.
 
• It was aimed at preventing the press from criticizing British policies, particularly during the **Second Anglo-Afghan War**.

questions.question: Which of the following committees, in its 2009 report, is known for introducing a widely used method to estimate poverty levels in India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Suresh Tendulkar Committee**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Suresh Tendulkar Committee** was constituted by the **Planning Commission** in **2005** to review the methodology for poverty estimation; it submitted its highly influential report in **2009**.
 
• The committee moved away from the traditional **calorie-based poverty estimation** model, which had been the standard since the **Lakdawala Committee**, and shifted toward a **private expenditure** approach based on consumption.
 
• It introduced a more comprehensive **Poverty Line Basket (PLB)** that included essential expenditures on **health** and **education**, marking a significant departure from previous models that focused primarily on food intake.
 
• The committee recommended the use of **Mixed Reference Period (MRP)** based estimates, which utilize a **365-day recall period** for infrequent purchases like clothing and durables, and a **30-day recall period** for food items.
 
• Under this methodology, the poverty line was calculated as a **Monthly Per Capita Expenditure (MPCE)**, determining that **37.2 percent** of the Indian population lived below the poverty line in **2004-05**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Rangarajan Expert Group**:

 
 
• Constituted in **2012** to address criticisms of the Tendulkar methodology, it submitted its findings in **2014**.
 
• It suggested a higher poverty line and recommended a modified **calorie-protein-fat** consumption requirement alongside non-food expenses.
 
 
 
• **Evolution of Poverty Estimation**:
 
 
• **Alagh Committee (1979)**: First to define a poverty line based on nutritional requirements (**2400 calories** for rural and **2100 calories** for urban areas).
 
• **Lakdawala Committee (1993)**: Introduced state-specific poverty lines based on the **Consumer Price Index for Agricultural Labourers (CPI-AL)** and **Consumer Price Index for Industrial Workers (CPI-IW)**.
 
• **NITI Aayog**: In **2015**, it replaced the Planning Commission and established a **Task Force on Elimination of Poverty** headed by **Arvind Panagariya** to further refine these metrics.

questions.question: Who took the oath as Bihar's Chief Minister for the record 10th time in 2025?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Shri Nitish Kumar**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Shri Nitish Kumar**, the leader of the **Janata Dal (United)** (JD-U), achieved a historic milestone by taking the oath as the **Chief Minister of Bihar** for a record **10th time** in **2025**.
 
• This event solidified his position as the politician with the most frequent swearings-in for the post of **Chief Minister** in the history of **Independent India**.
 
• The **Governor of Bihar** administered the **Oath of Office and Secrecy** to him at a ceremony held in **Raj Bhavan, Patna**.
 
• His political journey as the head of the state began in **March 2000**, and he has since led various **coalition governments** involving both the **National Democratic Alliance (NDA)** and the **Mahagathbandhan**.
 
• Under his leadership, the state has focused on the **Saat Nishchay** (Seven Resolves) program, aimed at providing basic amenities like electricity, drinking water, and infrastructure.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Tejashwi Prasad Yadav**:

 
 
• The younger son of **Lalu Prasad Yadav** and a key leader of the **Rashtriya Janata Dal (RJD)**.
 
• He has previously served as the **Deputy Chief Minister of Bihar** and currently acts as the **Leader of the Opposition**.
 
 
 
• **Lalu Prasad Yadav**:
 
 
• A veteran Indian politician and the founder-president of the **RJD**.
 
• He served as the **Chief Minister of Bihar** from **1990 to 1997** and was the **Union Railway Minister** (2004–2009).
 
 
 
• **Constitutional Framework**:
 
 
• **Article 164**: Specifies that the **Chief Minister** shall be appointed by the **Governor**, and other ministers shall be appointed on the advice of the **CM**.
 
• The **Chief Minister** acts as the **Chairman of the State Planning Board** and the chief spokesperson of the State Government.
 
 
 
• **Shri Nishant Kumar** is the son of Nitish Kumar but has remained largely **inactive in mainstream politics**.

questions.question: Allocation of seats to States and Union Territories in the Rajya Sabha is provided under which of the following Schedules of the Constitution of India?​
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Fourth Schedule**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Fourth Schedule** of the **Constitution of India** specifically details the **allocation of seats** in the **Rajya Sabha** (the Council of States) to each **State** and **Union Territory**.
 
• This allocation is fundamentally governed by the provisions of **Article 4(1)** and **Article 80(2)** of the Constitution.
 
• The number of representatives from each state in the **Rajya Sabha** depends mainly on the **population** of that state; for instance, **Uttar Pradesh** holds the highest number of seats due to its large demographic size.
 
• The schedule is subject to amendments whenever new states are created or existing states are reorganized through acts of **Parliament**, such as the **Andhra Pradesh Reorganisation Act** or the **Jammu and Kashmir Reorganisation Act**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Sixth Schedule**:

 
 
• Contains provisions related to the administration of **tribal areas** in the four northeastern states: **Assam**, **Meghalaya**, **Tripura**, and **Mizoram**.
 
• It allows for the creation of **Autonomous District Councils** to protect the rights of tribal populations.
 
 
 
• **Eighth Schedule**:
 
 
• Lists the **22 official languages** recognized by the **Constitution of India**.
 
• Originally, it contained 14 languages, but others like **Sindhi**, **Konkani**, **Manipuri**, **Nepali**, **Bodo**, **Dogri**, **Maithili**, and **Santhali** were added via various **Constitutional Amendment Acts**.
 
 
 
• **Tenth Schedule**:
 
 
• Popularly known as the **Anti-Defection Law**, it was added by the **52nd Amendment Act, 1985**.
 
• It sets the criteria for the **disqualification** of members of **Parliament** and **State Legislatures** if they defect from one political party to another.

questions.question: Which of the following renowned Indian musicians performed at the Red Fort on the occasion of India’s independence in 1947?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Ustad Bismillah Khan**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• On **August 15, 1947**, **Ustad Bismillah Khan** became the first Indian to greet the independent nation with his **Shehnai** from the ramparts of the **Red Fort** in **Delhi**.
 
• He was personally invited by the first Prime Minister of India, **Jawaharlal Nehru**, to perform on this historic occasion, which took place immediately after the **'Tryst with Destiny'** speech.
 
• The maestro performed **Raag Kafi**, a melodic mode in **Hindustani Classical Music**, symbolizing a new dawn for the country.
 
• Prior to his contribution, the **Shehnai** was largely relegated to temples and weddings as an accompaniment; he is credited with elevating it to the status of a prestigious **classical concert instrument**.
 
• His performance at the **Red Fort** established a tradition where his recorded **Shehnai** music is played every year on **Independence Day** before the Prime Minister's address.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Ustad Bismillah Khan**:

 
 
• Born in **Dumraon, Bihar**, he was awarded the **Bharat Ratna** in **2001**, making him one of the few musicians to receive India's highest civilian honor.
 
 
 
• **Pandit Ravi Shankar**:
 
 
• A world-renowned **Sitar** virtuoso and composer who introduced Indian music to the Western world and received the **Bharat Ratna** in **1999**.
 
 
 
• **Pandit Hariprasad Chaurasia**:
 
 
• An eminent classical flautist who plays the **Bansuri** (bamboo flute) and is a recipient of the **Padma Vibhushan**.
 
 
 
• **Pandit Bhimsen Joshi**:
 
 
• A legendary vocalist of the **Kirana Gharana**, known for his mastery of the **Khayal** style of singing; he was awarded the **Bharat Ratna** in **2008**.

questions.question: Which of the following is the primary objective of Mission Sudarshan Chakra, launched by India in August 2025?

options.text: Create a powerful defence weapon system

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Create a powerful defence weapon system**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Mission Sudarshan Chakra** was officially launched in **August 2025** as a flagship initiative to overhaul India's **strategic deterrence** capabilities.
 
• The primary objective of this mission is the indigenous development and deployment of a **powerful defence weapon system** that integrates **hypersonic technology** and **artificial intelligence**.
 
• It aims to provide a **multi-layered shield** against long-range ballistic missiles and sophisticated aerial intrusions, ensuring **national security**.
 
• The mission is spearheaded by the **Defence Research and Development Organisation (DRDO)** in collaboration with various **Indian private sector** defense giants.
 
• This initiative is a critical component of the **Atmanirbhar Bharat** (Self-Reliant India) vision, specifically targeting a reduction in dependency on foreign **military hardware**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Defence Weapon Systems**:

 
 
• Focuses on **Directed Energy Weapons (DEWs)** and advanced **Electronic Warfare (EW)** suites.
 
• Includes the development of **interceptor missiles** with high-altitude terminal phase neutralization capacity.
 
• Enhances **situational awareness** through a network of **Low Earth Orbit (LEO)** satellites.
 
 
 
• **Strategic Significance**:
 
 
• Strengthens India's position in the **Indo-Pacific region** by modernizing its **tactical arsenal**.
 
• Promotes **dual-use technology** research that can potentially benefit high-end precision manufacturing.
 
• Ensures a **credible minimum deterrence** posture in an evolving global security landscape.

questions.question: Who became the first Indian senior world champion in speed skating by winning the 1,000 m sprint at the World Championships in September 2025?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Anandkumar Velkumar**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Anandkumar Velkumar** made history by becoming the **first Indian athlete** to clinch a **gold medal** in the **senior category** at the **World Speed Skating Championships**.
 
• He achieved this feat in the **1,000 m sprint** event, held in **September 2025**, marking a paradigm shift for **Indian roller sports** on the international stage.
 
• The **1,000 m sprint** is a high-intensity track race that requires a precise combination of **aerobic endurance**, **anaerobic power**, and tactical maneuvering during the final laps.
 
• Prior to this victory, India had achieved success primarily in the **junior divisions**, making this **senior world title** a landmark achievement for the **Roller Skating Federation of India (RSFI)**.
 
• His performance at the championships reflects the growing infrastructure and professional training standards for **speed skating** within India, particularly in states like **Tamil Nadu** and **Karnataka**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Speed Skating Fundamentals**:

 
 
• The sport involves racing on **inline skates** (featuring wheels in a single line) on specialized **banked tracks** or flat road circuits.
 
• Key distances in championships include the **200 m Dual Time Trial**, **500 m + Distance**, and the **10,000 m Elimination** race.
 
 
 
• **Other Notable Skaters**:
 
 
• **Dhanush Babu**: A prominent Indian skater known for multiple **national records** and representational success in **Asian championships**.
 
• **Vikram Ingale** and **Aryanpal Singh Ghuman**: Part of the **Indian relay team** that secured medals at the **2022 Asian Games**, contributing to the sport's rising popularity.
 
 
 
• **Governance and Recognition**:
 
 
• **World Skate**: The global governing body for all roller sports, recognized by the **International Olympic Committee (IOC)**.
 
• The **Roller Skating Federation of India (RSFI)**: Established in **1955**, it oversees the development and selection of athletes for major events like the **Asian Games** and **World Championships**.

questions.question: Which of the following Directive Principles was NOT added to the Indian Constitution as part of the 42ⁿd Amendment Act of 1976?

options.text: Article 39A: To promote equal justice and to provide free legal aid to the poor
Article 48A: To protect and improve the environment and safeguard forests and wildlife
Article 38: State to minimise inequalities in income, status, facilities and opportunities
Article 39: To secure opportunities for healthy development of children

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Article 38: State to minimise inequalities in income, status, facilities and opportunities**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Article 39A** was inserted into the **Indian Constitution** by the **42ⁿd Amendment Act of 1976**. It directs the State to ensure that the operation of the legal system promotes justice on a basis of **equal opportunity** and provides **free legal aid** to ensure that opportunities for securing justice are not denied to any citizen by reason of economic or other disabilities. Hence, statement 1 is correct.
 
• **Article 48A** was added by the **42ⁿd Amendment Act of 1976** under the **Directive Principles of State Policy (DPSP)**. This article mandates that the State shall endeavour to protect and improve the **environment** and to safeguard the **forests** and **wildlife** of the country. Hence, statement 2 is correct.
 
• **Article 38** originally existed in the Constitution, but its second clause, which requires the State to **minimise inequalities in income** and eliminate inequalities in **status, facilities, and opportunities**, was inserted by the **44th Amendment Act of 1978** during the Morarji Desai-led government. Hence, statement 3 is incorrect.
 
• **Article 39** clause (f) was amended by the **42ⁿd Amendment Act of 1976**. It emphasizes that children should be given opportunities and facilities to develop in a healthy manner and in conditions of **freedom and dignity**, protecting them against **exploitation** and moral and material abandonment. Hence, statement 4 is correct.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **42ⁿd Constitutional Amendment Act (1976)**:

 
 
• Commonly referred to as the **Mini-Constitution** due to its massive scope of changes.
 
• It added three new words to the **Preamble**: **Socialist**, **Secular**, and **Integrity**.
 
• It introduced **Fundamental Duties** for citizens by adding **Part IV-A** (Article 51A).
 
• It added four new Directive Principles: **Article 39** (f), **Article 39A**, **Article 43A** (Participation of workers in management), and **Article 48A**.
 
 
 
• **44th Constitutional Amendment Act (1978)**:
 
 
• Enacted to nullify several provisions introduced by the 42ⁿd Amendment during the Emergency.
 
• It removed the **Right to Property** from the list of **Fundamental Rights** and made it a **Legal Right** under **Article 300A**.
 
• It substituted the words 'internal disturbance' with '**armed rebellion**' in respect of **National Emergency** (Article 352).

questions.question: Which of the following successfully conducted user trials of the Akash-NG missile?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Defence Research and Development Organisation (DRDO)**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Defence Research and Development Organisation (DRDO)** successfully conducted the flight trial of the **New Generation Akash (Akash-NG)** missile from the **Integrated Test Range (ITR)**, **Chandipur**, off the coast of **Odisha**.
 
• The **Akash-NG** is a state-of-the-art **Surface-to-Air Missile (SAM)** system specifically designed for the **Indian Air Force (IAF)** to intercept high-speed, agile aerial threats with low radar signatures.
 
• The flight test was conducted against a high-speed unmanned aerial target at a very low altitude, successfully validating the functioning of the complete weapon system, including the **missile**, **indigenous seeker**, and **launcher**.
 
• The missile system features a **dual-pulse solid rocket motor**, which significantly enhances its speed and provides an operational range of approximately **70 to 80 kilometers**.
 
• It is equipped with an **Active Electronically Scanned Array (AESA)** multi-function radar that provides the capability to track and engage multiple targets from various directions simultaneously.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Bharat Electronics Limited (BEL)**:

 
 
• A **Navratna Public Sector Undertaking (PSU)** under the **Ministry of Defence**.
 
• It acts as the lead integrator for the production of **radar systems** and electronic components for the **Akash** missile family.
 
 
 
• **Hindustan Aeronautics Limited (HAL)**:
 
 
• Headquartered in **Bengaluru**, it is a premier aerospace company.
 
• Focuses on the design and manufacture of **fighter jets** like **Tejas**, **helicopters**, and **gas turbine engines**.
 
 
 
• **Mazagon Dock Shipbuilders Limited**:
 
 
• Located in **Mumbai**, it is India's leading shipyard.
 
• Specializes in the construction of **destroyers**, **stealth frigates**, and **Scorpene-class submarines** for the **Indian Navy**.
